recent.summary: CoreWeave's 168% revenue beat reignited the AI infrastructure trade, driving broad semiconductor gains with MU +11.9%, ORCL +8.8%, and INTC +7.5%, while TSM and MU BUYs are well in the money. NVDA surged +2.87% intraday but collapsed ~8% after-hours on multi-source reports of a board vote to remove CEO Jensen Huang, keeping the open SELL from $178.67 firmly in profit. Mega-cap tech (MSFT, META, AMZN) lagged badly on a broadly green tape, reinforcing persistent relative weakness and active SELL signals in those names.

Jensen Huang's abrupt NVDA CEO resignation is the dominant catalyst, sending NVDA down 4.3% while AMD and AVGO surge ~5.5-5.9% on rotation into alternative semis; the open NVDA SELL from $178.67 is now +7.0% in favor. Crypto-adjacent names (MSTR -6.5%, MARA -6.0%) are cratering under rising yield pressure alongside a Microsoft outage dragging mega-cap tech, keeping broad indices in the red. Energy names (XOM +1.84%) caught a bid from a Houthi attack on a Saudi pipeline, while AVGO and GOOGL emerge as the cleanest new BUY setups amid persistent AI infrastructure demand.

A risk-off wave swept the AI/semiconductor complex for a third consecutive day, driven by the NVDA CEO resignation fallout and an HSBC sector downgrade, pushing AMD -8.75%, AVGO -4.76%, and NVDA lower while capital rotated into defensives like WMT, CVX, and META. Active SELL signals on NVDA (+8.8%) and AMD (+8.8%) are deep in the money, while the META SELL from $628.77 has flipped to a loss and warrants closing. Energy names caught a geopolitical bid from simultaneous Reuters reports of Iranian IRGC tanker mine strikes in the Hormuz Strait and Houthi missile attacks on Saudi forces, reinforcing the CVX BUY thesis.

A new US rule curbing China's access to AI chips (Reuters/CNBC) triggered a broad risk-off selloff, crushing semiconductors and AI names — Nasdaq fell 2.5% with NVDA, MU, AVGO, and AI ticker all down 4–10%. Defensive rotation into healthcare (UNH +1.1%) and consumer staples (COST +0.7%, WMT +0.25%) were the only bright spots in an almost entirely red 30-stock universe. NVDA's Tuesday earnings remain a binary risk event compounded by ongoing CEO succession uncertainty following Jensen Huang's exit, while open SELL signals on NVDA (+12.6%) and AMD (+13.8%) continue to outperform a struggling BUY book (37% hit rate).

A broad risk-off wave is crushing AI/software (CRM -9.5%), healthcare (UNH -5.4% on CMS Medicare Advantage clawback), and crypto-adjacent names (MSTR -6.3%) as VIX surges for a fourth consecutive day and a generational rotation from tech to defensives accelerates. Defense (RTX, LMT) and diversified semis (AVGO +2.5%) are the sole survivors, buoyed by dual Middle East escalation events (US strikes on Qeshm Island, Bahrain intercepts) and an NVDA earnings beat validating AI infrastructure demand. Key signals include high-confidence SELLs on NVDA (export curb + CEO uncertainty) and UNH (regulatory liability flip), with new BUYs initiated on RTX, AVGO, and AMZN (White House AI champion designation + Anthropic IPO optionality).

Anthropic's record $81.3B IPO dominated the session, lifting AI/cloud and semi names (NET +5.7%, AMD +5.3%, AMZN +3.8%, AVGO +3.6%) while NVDA fell -2.9% as post-CEO-exit governance concerns offset an earnings beat. Energy cratered on US-Iran oil transfer curbs (XOM/CVX/OXY all ~-4–5%), UNH collapsed -10.2% on CMS Medicare Advantage clawback proposals, and crypto-adjacent names sold off on hawkish Fed October minutes signaling more rate hikes. Broad indices barely moved as intense sector rotation offset gains and losses.

A broad risk-off selloff accelerated into a 6th consecutive S&P 500 decline, with the AI/semiconductor complex hit hardest by a triple catalyst: a Hunterbrook short-seller report linking AMD firmware to a blacklisted Chinese firm (-7.7%), a California AG subpoena adding legal/governance overhang to NVDA (-ongoing), and Anthropic's IPO pop failing to revive the AI trade. SELL discipline dominated the session with NVDA SELL +6.5% in favor and UNH SELL +15.2%, while only CVX held green on Middle East energy risk premium from a Houthi strike on Riyadh. BUY positions in AVGO, AMZN, and COST are holding but underwater pressure is mounting across the full book.

weekly.summary: A BofA AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit stress, and VIX spiking above 22 triggered a four-session, $260B+ risk-off unwind crushing high-multiple AI, cloud, and crypto names (PLTR, SNOW -8%+, MSTR -9.6% with added MSCI removal headwinds, MARA -9.6%). Capital rotated decisively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation, while AAPL held as the lone resilient core-tech name on iPhone demand, Chinese subsidies, and Berkshire support. Core calls — **BUY RTX, LMT, AAPL; SELL PLTR, MSTR** — remained fully intact across all sessions.

**Week Summary (3 sentences):**

AI/cloud and cybersecurity (DDOG, NET, AMZN) were the dominant BUY themes, fueled by SpaceX compute demand, PHP vulnerability spikes, and Iran escalation-driven infrastructure bids — with NET and DDOG delivering strong gains — though the Nasdaq's worst session since June, triggered by chipmaking supply warnings and META AI spending fears, crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and pulled the broader growth complex below its 50-day MA. Defense was a major early-week driver via NOC's $110B backlog, LMT's ~7% F-35 surge, and RTX read-across BUYs, but geopolitical risk-premium fading and Ukraine peace talk resumption sparked a late-week rotation out of the sector, while capital shifted defensively into cybersecurity and energy infrastructure as Iran escalation entered day two. MSTR and PLTR SELLs were badly burned (-12.2% and -8.4%) by crypto regulatory clarity and the AI rebound, AAPL was downgraded on foldable sell-the-news risk, and AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings — leaving NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) as the week's cleanest working calls.

**Summary:** AI infrastructure euphoria rapidly reversed into a sector-wide reckoning — early BUY validation from ORCL, Azure, and Anthropic's IPO gave way to INTC's -28.6% collapse, GOOGL's worst-ever single-day drop (-12.6%) on structural search fears, and broad semi weakness (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, DDOG all deeply underwater), leaving the Nasdaq on pace for its worst month in over a year. Capital rotated decisively into Defense (LHX +6.84%, RTX, LMT outperforming on $11B missile awards and DoD spending), Energy (XOM, CVX bid up on Hormuz tanker fires and Saudi evacuation orders), and Consumer Staples (WMT), while Big Tech earnings sharply divided the tape with AMZN on WATCH amid AI capex overhang. Key active calls are BUY LHX, RTX, LLY; high-conviction SELL GOOGL and META; a hawkish Fed hold at 3.75–4.0% and tighter sell discipline on AI longs represent the principal forward risks.

**Summary:** The two-week period was dominated by extreme semiconductor volatility — an initial brutal chip selloff (MU -17.5%, AMD -17.3%, TSM -10.8%) driven by AI spending fears and regulation concerns was followed by a sharp rebound (AMD +11%, TSM +6.3%) confirming AI capex demand remains intact, while mega-cap tech (MSFT, AAPL) and post-election defensives lagged the recovery. Key calls saw AMZN emerge as the standout long (+8.3%), PLTR SELL extend gains to +11.6%, AMD BUY cut at -16.4% loss, and MSFT BUY exited on a fresh negative catalyst, with NVDA re-entered at oversold levels into the bounce. Overall portfolio conviction remains cautious with a challenged 47%/33% win rate, as cloud earnings risk (DDOG -14.4%) and ongoing sector rotation complexity continue to pressure execution.

**Weekly Summary (2 Weeks)**

Markets whipsawed between a broad risk-on surge (Dow +1,100+) driving semiconductor and AI gains — AMD +13.3% on a Google Cloud win, NET +9.3% on a strong earnings beat, AVGO +8.8% — and a subsequent risk-off reversal triggered by a hotter-than-expected CPI print reigniting 50bps Fed hike fears, with NVDA the standout loser across both weeks (-4.3% then -5.5%) after a CEO governance probe prompted a SELL flip. Defensives (LMT +2.5%) and crypto (MARA +10.5%) diverged from the broader tech selloff, while NET/TSM showed resilience on fundamentals versus COIN's underperformance highlighting exchange-specific rate sensitivity. Key discipline takeaways: require multi-source confirmation before entering BUY signals, treat leadership/governance risk as an immediate exit trigger, and size down high-multiple AI names into yield-surge environments.
